title: One melody, ever more extravagant
work: Nocturne in E♭ major, Op. 9 No. 2
question: How do Lévy and Prati keep the tune singing as its ornaments grow more elaborate?
intro: Frank Lévy and Patrizia Prati play a song that keeps inventing new ways to sing. A leap from B♭ to G begins it, over the left hand’s rocking bass and chords. Each return gathers more ornaments, until a tiny cadenza sends the melody spinning free.

recordings.label: Frank Lévy, c. 2014
recordings.note: A pupil of Maria Tipo and Leon Fleisher, Lévy made this recording for Musopen’s Chopin project.

recordings.label: Patrizia Prati, 2015
recordings.note: Prati recorded twelve Chopin nocturnes at Madrid’s Museum of Romanticism on 24 November 2015.

passages.label: Melody and accompaniment
passages.note: The melody hangs above the left hand’s recurring bass note and two answering chords.

passages.label: The phrase settles
passages.note: A leap into the treble is answered by a falling run; the phrase settles back onto E♭.

passages.label: A trill in the song
passages.note: A trill catches on a held note before the melody resumes its descent. The left hand keeps the same rocking pattern.

passages.label: The ornamented line
passages.note: The tune returns with small, quick notes wound around its longer ones. The bass retraces its familiar route.

passages.label: Two notes at a time
passages.note: Paired notes thicken the right-hand melody, then short, detached chords draw the phrase towards its next return.

passages.label: The last ascent
passages.note: The right hand climbs into octaves as the music gathers force. The cadenza is close.

passages.label: E♭ after the cadenza
passages.note: The cadenza has spent itself. Softly rolling E♭-major chords restore the pulse and lead into the final hush.
